- Overestimate prices in bullish sentiment periods (high sentiment > 0.3) — reduce forecast by 1–2% for 3–5 day horizons.
- Underestimate prices after strong downward spikes (sentiment < 0.1) — add 0.5–1.5% to forecast to avoid underreaction.
- Avoid over-optimism in early forecast windows (1–3 days) — cap forecast at 1.5–2% below recent 7-day average.
- When sentiment is volatile (alternating 0.1–0.4), reduce forecast variance — use 3-day moving average for smoothing.
- For 10+ day horizons, apply mean reversion: if forecast > 20% above recent 30-day mean, reduce by 10–15%.
- If sentiment is consistently low (avg < 0.15) over 3+ days, forecast should not exceed 1.2x recent 14-day high — avoid overbought bias.
- Correct for lag: if forecast is > 1.5% above true outcome at day 1–3, adjust downward by 0.5–1.0% per day until convergence.
